column1: # Candidate repositories for the corpus that are not in it yet.
# Two batches, both filtered to repos that are not archived, not forks, and
#   1. Herb adopters, discovered with `bin/corpus discover` (GitHub code
#      search for .herb.yml, @herb-tools in package.json, and gem "herb" in
#      a Gemfile). GitHub's REST code search cannot do path globs, so this
#      relies on filename:/extension: plus a free-text term.
#   2. A path-based sweep for `**/*.html.erb` and `**/.herb.yml` via the
#      Sourcegraph public search API, which does support path regexes:
#      Capped at repos with >= 50 .html.erb files, then deduped against
#      corpus.yml by canonical repo name so renames (thepracticaldev/dev.to
#      -> forem/forem) do not sneak back in as duplicates.
# Columns: repo, branch, license, redistributable, name
# Blank branch means detect the default. Unverified licenses are marked
# redistributable=false so nothing ships until someone reads the license.
# erb counts at time of discovery are in the trailing comment on each row.
# 4,219 public repos contain .html.erb and 347 contain .rhtml, which Herb
# parses the same way. 4,052 of those were new. Capped at >= 50 templates
# (.html.erb + .rhtml) per repo, then dropped 9 already in the corpus under
# a renamed slug, 4 archived, and 3 that carry a .herb.yml but ship no
# The counts below are every **/*.erb and **/*.rhtml on the default branch,
# from the git tree API; a trailing + means the tree response was truncated
# so the count is a floor.
